sections.title: loopctl (report section 10; python3 .claude/scripts/loopctl <command>)
comment: loopctl owns the deterministic decisions of the loop: state, counters, caps, the lock, spend, abort.
Read from the BASE sha by loopctl, never from the branch it is judging (CO-11).

keys.name: runner
doc: sequential | driver   (report section 11.2, DEC-23). Where an item runs. Never auto-selected.
sequential = the prose loop: the Orchestrator conductor dispatches engineers itself; `loopctl run` prints the
hand-off and exits (default)
driver     = `loopctl run` launches one `claude -p` child per item or stage (OPT-IN, needs loopctl_tier2: true,
run_budget_usd > 0 and the driver module)
the Orchestrator runs the loop in my session

keys.name: loopctl_tier2
doc: OPT-IN (experimental, IMP-1). Tier 2 = the loopctl commands that write loop state: begin, advance, fail, approve,
gate, run, abort, reconcile --apply. They refuse while this is false. Tier 1 (validate, status, render, doctor,
migrate-plan, lock, evidence, cost, audit, halt, resume) works either way. It is not evidence-gated: three clean
runs with loopctl are what the evidence gate asks for.
leave off until you want loopctl to own the item state

keys.name: run_budget_usd
doc: USD ceiling for one run, summed from each child session's total_cost_usd (report section 10.5). 0 = not set.
Set it explicitly before `runner: driver` (no projection exists before a baseline). Reaching it parks the run.
0 = not set; the driver refuses to start until you set a ceiling

keys.name: item_budget_usd
doc: USD ceiling for one item across its attempts. 0 = not set. Reaching it sets the item needs_human.

keys.name: day_budget_usd
doc: USD ceiling per UTC day over every run in this repository. 0 = not set.

keys.name: lock_stale_min
doc: Minutes without a heartbeat before the run lock may be stolen (report section 19.7). The owner must also be
gone: the driver pid dead, or the session not registered. A lock from another host is never stolen unless
you say `lock steal --host-dead`.

keys.name: max_transient_retries
doc: Retries of a `transient` failure (flaky test, port in use) per item attempt. Each one also uses retry budget.

keys.name: max_platform_retries
doc: Retries of a `platform` failure (API 5xx, overloaded, rate limit, CLI crash) per item, with backoff and jitter.
They do not use retry budget; past this number the item is parked as needs_human (an outage, not a bug).

keys.name: platform_backoff_base_s
doc: Seconds before the first platform retry; it doubles each time, with jitter, up to 15 minutes.

keys.name: dispatch_timeout_min
doc: Minutes without a tool call before a dispatched session counts as stalled (a `transient` failure). Read by the
driver; loopctl classifies the stall.

keys.name: orphan_retention_days
doc: Days a `dead/*` branch is kept before `reconcile --apply` prunes it. `blocked/*` is never auto-deleted.

keys.name: state_remote
doc: Name of the git remote that also holds refs/loopctl/state/<plan>. Empty = local only (L1). At L2 and above set it:
state is then written with a compare-and-swap push, so it survives a fresh clone. Advisory, not a boundary:
anyone with contents: write can move the ref. Empty or a remote name; never a URL.

keys.name: db_migrate_down
doc: Command that runs ONE down-migration against the local or ephemeral database (report section 19.7 L-25). It gets
LOOPCTL_ITEM, LOOPCTL_MIGRATION and LOOPCTL_MIGRATION_DOWN in its environment, never on its command line.
Empty = `loopctl abort` writes the down-migrations into the human revert plan instead of running them.
